title: Quantifying Epigenetic Changes Induced by Chemical Exposure Using the epi-TK Assay
author: Shiro Kuroki

materials: Human lymphoblastoid mTK6 cell line (TK6-derived cell line originally established in a previous study [6]; available from the authors upon request), stored at -80 °C for short-term storage or in liquid nitrogen for long-term storage. Alternatively, equivalent cell lines can be established from the parental TK6 cell line or other cell types by isolating TFT-resistant clones generated via transient expression of dCas9-DNMT3A with guide RNAs targeting the TK gene promoter [6]. steps.title: Seed initial mTK6 culture
steps.instruction: Seed mTK6 cells at 30,000 cells / mL in a 15‑cm culture dish containing RPMI‑1640 complete medium.

steps.title: Add TFT and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of 1,000× TFT solution per 1 mL of culture medium (final 1/1,000 volume) and incubate for 3 days at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Check morphology and count
steps.instruction: Examine cell morphology and contamination with an inverted microscope, transfer the suspension to a 50‑mL conical tube, and determine cell number using a Z2 particle counter or counting chamber.

steps.title: Adjust density and reseed
steps.instruction: Dilute the culture to a density of 200,000–300,000 cells / mL, seed the cells into a new 15‑cm dish with fresh RPMI‑1640 complete medium, add TFT at 1/1,000 of the final volume, and incubate an additional 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Transfer culture for exposure
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire culture volume to a 50‑mL conical tube and determine cell density; aim for approximately 800,000–1,000,000 cells / mL.

steps.title: Collect cells for treatment
steps.instruction: Based on the measured density, transfer a volume containing (number of treated groups + 1) × 2,500,000 cells into a new 50‑mL conical tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard medium
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, carefully discard the supernatant (RPMI‑1640 complete medium with TFT), and gently tap the tube to loosen the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend in fresh medium
steps.instruction: Add fresh RPMI‑1640 complete medium without TFT at a volume of (number of treated groups + 1) × 5 mL, then resuspend the cells thoroughly.

steps.title: Adjust to 500 k cells/mL
steps.instruction: Measure cell density again and adjust the suspension to 500,000 ± 5 % cells / mL (i.e., 475,000–525,000 cells / mL).

steps.title: Aliquot and add test reagent
steps.instruction: Aliquot 5.0 mL of the cell suspension into each 15‑mL conical tube, add 4.9 mL fresh RPMI‑1640 complete medium, then add 100 µL of the test reagent (e.g., GSK‑3484862) to achieve final concentrations of 0.5, 2, or 5 µM, or add 100 µL DMSO as vehicle control. For compounds with unknown cytotoxicity, first evaluate a range starting at 10 mM (or 2 mg / mL if molecular weight > 200) using serial 10‑fold dilutions.

steps.title: Incubate treated cultures
steps.instruction: Transfer the contents of each 15‑mL tube to a 10‑cm culture dish by decanting and incubate for 24 h at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Harvest cells from dishes
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire cell suspension from each 10‑cm dish into a 15‑mL conical tube and centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: First wash
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, add 5 mL RPMI‑1640 complete medium, mix by gentle inversion, and centrifuge again at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Second wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the wash step (add 5 mL RPMI‑1640 complete medium, invert, centrifuge 500 × g, 5 min, 4 °C).

steps.title: Resuspend and count
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, gently loosen the pellet, resuspend cells in RPMI‑1640 complete medium, and determine cell density with a Z2 particle counter or counting chamber.

steps.title: Adjust to 200 k cells/mL
steps.instruction: Adjust each treatment group to approximately 200,000 cells / mL in a total volume of 10 mL using fresh RPMI‑1640 complete medium.

steps.title: Prepare vehicle control dilutions
steps.instruction: For the vehicle control: (a) start with 200,000 cells / mL, 10 mL; (b) dilute to 5,000 cells / mL by mixing 1.25 mL of the starting suspension with 48.75 mL RPMI‑1640 complete medium (total 50 mL); (c) dilute to 200 cells / mL by mixing 0.40 mL of the 5,000‑cell suspension with 9.6 mL RPMI‑1640 complete medium (total 10 mL); (d) prepare the cloning‑efficiency (CE) suspension at 8 cells / mL by mixing 1.0 mL of the 200‑cell suspension with 24 mL RPMI‑1640 complete medium (total 25 mL).

steps.title: Prepare GSK‑treated dilutions
steps.instruction: For each GSK‑3484862‑treated group: (a) start with 200,000 cells / mL, 10 mL; (b) dilute to 5,000 cells / mL by mixing 0.10 mL of the starting suspension with 3.9 mL RPMI‑1640 complete medium (total 4 mL); (c) dilute to 100 cells / mL for revertant‑frequency (RF) plating by mixing 1.0 mL of the 5,000‑cell suspension with 49 mL RPMI‑1640 complete medium (total 50 mL); (d) prepare the CE suspension at 8 cells / mL by mixing 2.0 mL of the 100‑cell suspension with 23 mL RPMI‑1640 complete medium (total 25 mL). For compounds with unknown epigenetic activity, preliminarily test RF plating densities ranging from 100 to 100,000 cells / mL using serial 10‑fold dilutions.

steps.title: Add CHAT solution
steps.instruction: Add 100× CHAT solution at 1 % of the final culture volume prepared for RF plating (e.g., 500 µL for the vehicle‑control tube and 485 µL for each GSK‑treated tube, based on their respective final volumes).

steps.title: Seed 96‑well plates
steps.instruction: Transfer the RF or CE cell suspensions to reagent reservoirs and dispense 200 µL per well into 96‑well flat‑bottom plates using a P200L multichannel pipette.

steps.title: Incubate plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the seeded plates for 3 weeks at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Mark wells with color change
steps.instruction: Place each plate on a white background, identify wells where the medium has changed from red to yellow, and mark those wells as potentially containing colonies.

steps.title: Confirm colonies microscopically
steps.instruction: Inspect every well under a stereomicroscope to confirm colony presence, especially in wells not marked by color change.

steps.title: Record colony numbers
steps.instruction: Record the number of positive (colonies present) and negative wells for both CE and RF plates according to the provided data tables.

steps.title: Calculate cloning efficiency
steps.instruction: Calculate cloning efficiency (CE) using CE = -ln(EW/TW) / N, where EW = number of wells without colonies, TW = total number of wells, and N = 1.6 cells per well for CE plates.

steps.title: Calculate revertant frequency
steps.instruction: Calculate revertant frequency (RF) using RF = [-ln(EW/TW) / N] / CE_treated, where N is the number of cells per well in the RF plates.

steps.title: Plot results
steps.instruction: Plot chemical concentration on the x‑axis versus relative survival (from CE) and TK revertant frequency on the y‑axis.

steps.title: Repeat and analyze statistically
steps.instruction: Repeat the entire experiment independently at least three times and perform statistical analysis using Dunnett’s test to compare each chemically‑treated group with the vehicle control.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been applied and validated in the following research article: Yamada et al. [6]. Dual-directional epi-genotoxicity assay for assessing chemically induced epigenetic effects utilizing the housekeeping TK gene. Scientific reports (Figure 2).
